record.Key_Distinction: Role identity is mechanical and cuts across distinct in-world traditions.
record.Source_Reference: Official Final Fantasy XIV race/clan pages and battle job guide.

record.Ontology_or_Role_Summary: Formal damage role combining mobility, ranged attacks, and party utility.
record.Power_Basis: Ranged weapons, songs, dances, devices, and support effects.
record.Key_Distinction: Bard, Machinist, and Dancer share a role but not a fictional profession.
record.Source_Reference: Official Final Fantasy XIV race/clan pages and battle job guide.

record.Ontology_or_Role_Summary: Formal damage role for spell-focused jobs with varied mobility and resource patterns.
record.Power_Basis: Casting, elemental or summon systems, and encounter timing.
record.Key_Distinction: Black Mage, Summoner, Red Mage, and Pictomancer are mechanically and fictionally distinct.
record.Source_Reference: Official Final Fantasy XIV race/clan pages and battle job guide.

record.Ontology_or_Role_Summary: A special job that learns monster actions and operates outside standard duty-role progression.
record.Power_Basis: Enemy-skill acquisition and separate content rules.
record.Key_Distinction: Its limited-job status is as important as its spell theme.
record.Source_Reference: Official Final Fantasy XIV race/clan pages and battle job guide.

record.Ontology_or_Role_Summary: Many jobs are accessed or embodied through soul crystals carrying accumulated techniques and memory.
record.Power_Basis: Artifact inheritance, training quests, and institutional lineage.
record.Key_Distinction: The crystal does not replace personal training; lore varies by job.
record.Source_Reference: Official Final Fantasy XIV race/clan pages and battle job guide.

record.Ontology_or_Role_Summary: High Elven people of Summerset with distinctive religious, political, and magical traditions.
record.Power_Basis: Natural ancestry, long life, culture, and history.
record.Key_Distinction: ‘High elf’ is a comparative label; Altmer identity is setting-specific.
record.Source_Reference: Franchise-spanning orientation; individual games and eras require continuity-specific verification.

record.Ontology_or_Role_Summary: Wood Elven people associated with Valenwood and the Green Pact.
record.Power_Basis: Natural ancestry, ecological covenant, and culture.
record.Key_Distinction: Not simply generic forest elves; dietary and religious obligations are central.
record.Source_Reference: Franchise-spanning orientation; individual games and eras require continuity-specific verification.

record.Ontology_or_Role_Summary: Dark Elven people of Morrowind shaped by ancestor religion, Great Houses, and historical transformations.
record.Power_Basis: Natural ancestry, divine history, culture, and politics.
record.Key_Distinction: ‘Dark elf’ here is not a moral category.
record.Source_Reference: Franchise-spanning orientation; individual games and eras require continuity-specific verification.

record.Ontology_or_Role_Summary: The Orc people, metaphysically connected to elven history and organized in varied stronghold and urban cultures.
record.Power_Basis: Ancestry, transformation myth, religion, and culture.
record.Key_Distinction: Their orc identity coexists with an elven-derived cosmological genealogy.
record.Source_Reference: Franchise-spanning orientation; individual games and eras require continuity-specific verification.

record.Ontology_or_Role_Summary: The vanished Deep Elves, conventionally called dwarves, renowned for tonal architecture and advanced constructs.
record.Power_Basis: Elven ancestry, subterranean civilization, technology, and disappearance.
record.Key_Distinction: They are not short Tolkien-style dwarves; the English nickname is historical.
record.Source_Reference: Franchise-spanning orientation; individual games and eras require continuity-specific verification.

record.Ontology_or_Role_Summary: Northern human people of Skyrim with diverse religious and political histories.
record.Power_Basis: Natural ancestry, regional culture, and mythic migration.
record.Key_Distinction: Not every Nord is a barbarian, warrior, or traditionalist.
record.Source_Reference: Franchise-spanning orientation; individual games and eras require continuity-specific verification.

record.Ontology_or_Role_Summary: Human peoples associated with Cyrodiil, imperial institutions, and multiple historical identities.
record.Power_Basis: Natural ancestry, state traditions, law, and cosmopolitan culture.
record.Key_Distinction: Imperial is partly political-cultural, not just biological.
record.Source_Reference: Franchise-spanning orientation; individual games and eras require continuity-specific verification.

record.Ontology_or_Role_Summary: Human people of High Rock with historical elven admixture and strong magical traditions.
record.Power_Basis: Ancestry, regional culture, and political fragmentation.
record.Key_Distinction: Their identity cannot be reduced to a stat bonus for magic resistance.
record.Comparative_Notes: Human–elder ancestry and feudal mage culture.
record.Source_Reference: Franchise-spanning orientation; individual games and eras require continuity-specific verification.

record.Ontology_or_Role_Summary: Human peoples of Hammerfell with Yokudan heritage and famed martial traditions.
record.Power_Basis: Natural ancestry, migration, religion, and regional cultures.
record.Key_Distinction: The sword tradition is only one aspect; samurai-derived is a loose functional comparison.
record.Comparative_Notes: Diasporic warrior and desert-kingdom human analogue.
record.Source_Reference: Franchise-spanning orientation; individual games and eras require continuity-specific verification.

record.Ontology_or_Role_Summary: A people whose many furstocks and body forms are linked to lunar conditions and culture.
record.Power_Basis: Natural ancestry, lunar metaphysics, and multiple morphologies.
record.Key_Distinction: Khajiit are not one catlike body plan or culture.
record.Source_Reference: Franchise-spanning orientation; individual games and eras require continuity-specific verification.

record.Ontology_or_Role_Summary: Reptilian people of Black Marsh with deep relationships to the Hist.
record.Power_Basis: Natural ancestry, communal culture, and symbiosis with sacred trees.
record.Key_Distinction: Their identity is not reducible to generic lizardfolk traits.
record.Comparative_Notes: Symbiotic marsh people and tree-linked ancestry.
record.Source_Reference: Franchise-spanning orientation; individual games and eras require continuity-specific verification.

record.Ontology_or_Role_Summary: Divine powers associated with creation and the structure of the mortal world.
record.Power_Basis: Cosmological participation, worship, and mythic interpretation.
record.Key_Distinction: Aedra is a relational theological category, not a biological species.
record.Source_Reference: Franchise-spanning orientation; individual games and eras require continuity-specific verification.

record.Ontology_or_Role_Summary: Powerful rulers of Oblivion realms embodying or governing distinct spheres.
record.Power_Basis: Otherworldly existence, realm sovereignty, cults, and artifacts.
record.Key_Distinction: They are not simply demons or uniformly evil.
record.Source_Reference: Franchise-spanning orientation; individual games and eras require continuity-specific verification.

record.Ontology_or_Role_Summary: Varied beings native or tied to realms of Oblivion.
record.Power_Basis: Otherworldly origin, summoning, contracts, and realm affiliations.
record.Key_Distinction: The category contains peoples, creatures, servants, and independent actors.
record.Source_Reference: Franchise-spanning orientation; individual games and eras require continuity-specific verification.

record.Ontology_or_Role_Summary: Ancient, intelligent dragons associated with time, domination, and the Thu'um.
record.Power_Basis: Draconic nature, language, immortality-like persistence, and divine origin.
record.Key_Distinction: They are not ordinary animals and their speech is itself power.
record.Source_Reference: Franchise-spanning orientation; individual games and eras require continuity-specific verification.

record.Ontology_or_Role_Summary: Mortals with a dragon soul or divinely significant draconic capacity, especially central to specific eras.
record.Power_Basis: Divine blessing, soul nature, prophecy, and learned shouts.
record.Key_Distinction: Not a species, and not the same concept as D&D dragonborn.
record.Source_Reference: Franchise-spanning orientation; individual games and eras require continuity-specific verification.

record.Ontology_or_Role_Summary: Reality-affecting power expressed through the dragon language and disciplined Shouts.
record.Power_Basis: Language, breath, understanding, and spiritual mastery.
record.Key_Distinction: More than sonic force; words carry ontological significance.
record.Source_Reference: Franchise-spanning orientation; individual games and eras require continuity-specific verification.

record.Ontology_or_Role_Summary: An ascetic order devoted to studying and regulating the Voice.
record.Power_Basis: Discipline, seclusion, oral teaching, and philosophical restraint.
record.Key_Distinction: They are an institution, not a class shared by all Voice users.
record.Source_Reference: Franchise-spanning orientation; individual games and eras require continuity-specific verification.

record.Ontology_or_Role_Summary: Ancient esoteric order devoted to metaphysical study and selective intervention.
record.Power_Basis: Training, secrecy, ritual, and philosophical tradition.
record.Key_Distinction: Its goals and methods vary by era and source.
record.Comparative_Notes: Hidden mage order and time-lore society.
record.Source_Reference: Franchise-spanning orientation; individual games and eras require continuity-specific verification.

record.Ontology_or_Role_Summary: An institution historically providing magical services, training, and regulation.
record.Power_Basis: Professional organization, education, commerce, and politics.
record.Key_Distinction: Its structure changes across eras and provinces.
record.Source_Reference: Franchise-spanning orientation; individual games and eras require continuity-specific verification.

record.Ontology_or_Role_Summary: A secretive assassination organization with a death-centered theology and contracts.
record.Power_Basis: Initiation, ritual, patronage, secrecy, and murder-for-hire.
record.Key_Distinction: Its religious claims and organizational continuity are contested within the setting.
record.Source_Reference: Franchise-spanning orientation; individual games and eras require continuity-specific verification.

record.Ontology_or_Role_Summary: Organized networks of thieves with codes, fences, patrons, and local politics.
record.Power_Basis: Criminal craft, mutual protection, and urban organization.
record.Key_Distinction: Different games depict different chapters and institutional strengths.
record.Source_Reference: Franchise-spanning orientation; individual games and eras require continuity-specific verification.

record.Ontology_or_Role_Summary: Multiple vampiric bloodlines and diseases granting powers alongside weaknesses.
record.Power_Basis: Infection or curse, bloodline, patronage, and transformation.
record.Key_Distinction: There is no single Elder Scrolls vampire template across eras and strains.
record.Comparative_Notes: Plural vampiric condition and lineage system.
record.Source_Reference: Franchise-spanning orientation; individual games and eras require continuity-specific verification.

record.Ontology_or_Role_Summary: Mortals transformed into predatory beast forms through disease, curse, or divine association.
record.Power_Basis: Transformation, infection, patronage, and beast-form abilities.
record.Key_Distinction: Multiple were-creature types exist beyond wolves.
record.Source_Reference: Franchise-spanning orientation; individual games and eras require continuity-specific verification.

record.Ontology_or_Role_Summary: One of several human civilizations and kingdoms in Azeroth.
record.Power_Basis: Natural ancestry, culture, state, and faction history.
record.Key_Distinction: Warcraft humans are culturally plural despite a single playable label.
record.Source_Reference: Official World of Warcraft race and class reference pages, version-stamped 2026-08-01.

record.Ontology_or_Role_Summary: Long-lived kaldorei people associated with ancient magic, forests, druidism, and lunar religion.
record.Power_Basis: Ancestry, historical transformation, culture, and divine ties.
record.Key_Distinction: They are not simply generic dark or wood elves.
record.Source_Reference: Official World of Warcraft race and class reference pages, version-stamped 2026-08-01.

record.Ontology_or_Role_Summary: Sin'dorei descended from high elves, shaped by magical catastrophe, addiction, and reconstruction.
record.Power_Basis: Ancestry, magical dependence, politics, and urban culture.
record.Key_Distinction: Their name records history and identity, not moral alignment.
record.Source_Reference: Official World of Warcraft race and class reference pages, version-stamped 2026-08-01.

record.Ontology_or_Role_Summary: Elves transformed or empowered through disciplined exposure to the Void.
record.Power_Basis: Ancestry plus hazardous metaphysical transformation.
record.Key_Distinction: They are not a wholly separate original species.
record.Source_Reference: Official World of Warcraft race and class reference pages, version-stamped 2026-08-01.

record.Ontology_or_Role_Summary: Titan-forged-descended peoples with multiple clans and archaeological traditions.
record.Power_Basis: Construct ancestry transformed into flesh, clan culture, craft, and history.
record.Key_Distinction: Their origin differs sharply from naturally evolved or Tolkienian dwarves.
record.Source_Reference: Official World of Warcraft race and class reference pages, version-stamped 2026-08-01.

record.Ontology_or_Role_Summary: Small titan-forged-descended people strongly associated with engineering and invention.
record.Power_Basis: Construct ancestry transformed into flesh, technology, and culture.
record.Key_Distinction: Engineering is culturally prominent but not an innate profession of every gnome.
record.Source_Reference: Official World of Warcraft race and class reference pages, version-stamped 2026-08-01.

record.Ontology_or_Role_Summary: A people from Draenor whose history includes clans, shamanism, demonic corruption, invasion, and renewal.
record.Power_Basis: Natural ancestry, clan culture, and historical magical corruption.
record.Key_Distinction: Their violent periods are historical and political, not proof of inherent evil.
record.Source_Reference: Official World of Warcraft race and class reference pages, version-stamped 2026-08-01.

record.Ontology_or_Role_Summary: Ancient and highly diverse peoples with many tribes, empires, religions, and adaptations.
record.Power_Basis: Natural ancestry, regional forms, loa traditions, and political history.
record.Key_Distinction: The playable label represents only some troll communities.
record.Comparative_Notes: Ancient tribal and imperial troll peoples.
record.Source_Reference: Official World of Warcraft race and class reference pages, version-stamped 2026-08-01.

record.Ontology_or_Role_Summary: Large bovine-featured people with spiritual, clan, and plains-based traditions.
record.Power_Basis: Natural ancestry, kinship, shamanic and druidic culture.
record.Key_Distinction: The horse-culture tag is only a loose mobility comparison; tauren are not horse peoples.
record.Source_Reference: Official World of Warcraft race and class reference pages, version-stamped 2026-08-01.

record.Ontology_or_Role_Summary: Self-aware undead communities freed from or resisting prior domination.
record.Power_Basis: Undeath, retained identity, political community, and contested autonomy.
record.Key_Distinction: They are a people and faction, not generic mindless zombies.
record.Source_Reference: Official World of Warcraft race and class reference pages, version-stamped 2026-08-01.

record.Ontology_or_Role_Summary: Long-lived eredar exiles associated with the Light, interworld travel, and technological relics.
record.Power_Basis: Otherworldly ancestry, faith, exile, and advanced artifice.
record.Key_Distinction: They are not angels despite visual and religious associations.
record.Source_Reference: Official World of Warcraft race and class reference pages, version-stamped 2026-08-01.

record.Ontology_or_Role_Summary: Panda-featured people with multiple philosophical, martial, and regional traditions.
record.Power_Basis: Natural ancestry, culture, and history.
record.Key_Distinction: Their presentation mixes comedy, martial philosophy, and serious political history.
record.Source_Reference: Official World of Warcraft race and class reference pages, version-stamped 2026-08-01.

record.Ontology_or_Role_Summary: Inventive goblin societies shaped by commerce, cartels, engineering, and risk-taking.
record.Power_Basis: Natural ancestry, economics, technology, and corporate institutions.
record.Key_Distinction: The profit-seeking stereotype is culturally specific and satirical, not biological essence.
record.Source_Reference: Official World of Warcraft race and class reference pages, version-stamped 2026-08-01.

record.Ontology_or_Role_Summary: Humans and related sufferers transformed by a controlled or inherited worgen curse.
record.Power_Basis: Curse, bodily transformation, social identity, and partial control.
record.Key_Distinction: A transformed population rather than an original wolf species.
record.Source_Reference: Official World of Warcraft race and class reference pages, version-stamped 2026-08-01.

record.Ontology_or_Role_Summary: Draconic humanoids created with multiple dragonflight powers and a humanoid visage.
record.Power_Basis: Engineered ancestry, draconic magic, training, and awakening.
record.Key_Distinction: They are distinct from dragonspawn, dragons, and ordinary humanoids.
record.Source_Reference: Official World of Warcraft race and class reference pages, version-stamped 2026-08-01.

record.Ontology_or_Role_Summary: Weapon-and-armor martial class spanning protection and damage specializations.
record.Power_Basis: Training, rage, equipment, and specialization.
record.Key_Distinction: The class is a rules family, not every soldier in the setting.
record.Source_Reference: Official World of Warcraft race and class reference pages, version-stamped 2026-08-01.

record.Ontology_or_Role_Summary: Ranged or beast-linked class using weapons, traps, tracking, and animal companions.
record.Power_Basis: Training, ranged weapons, pets, and specialization.
record.Key_Distinction: The mechanical Hunter includes multiple fictional vocations.
record.Source_Reference: Official World of Warcraft race and class reference pages, version-stamped 2026-08-01.

record.Ontology_or_Role_Summary: Light- or shadow-oriented spellcasting class with healing and damage specializations.
record.Power_Basis: Faith, psychic or sacred magic, and specialization.
record.Key_Distinction: The class joins multiple religions under one mechanical framework.
record.Source_Reference: Official World of Warcraft race and class reference pages, version-stamped 2026-08-01.

record.Ontology_or_Role_Summary: Learned arcane class specializing in fire, frost, or arcane magic.
record.Power_Basis: Study, arcane power, elemental schools, and specialization.
record.Key_Distinction: Not every setting mage uses this three-school structure.
record.Source_Reference: Official World of Warcraft race and class reference pages, version-stamped 2026-08-01.

record.Ontology_or_Role_Summary: Martial class using chi, brews, mobility, and healing or tank specializations.
record.Power_Basis: Training, chi traditions, martial technique, and specialization.
record.Key_Distinction: The class is strongly shaped by pandaren institutions but is learnable by many peoples.
record.Source_Reference: Official World of Warcraft race and class reference pages, version-stamped 2026-08-01.

record.Ontology_or_Role_Summary: Nature-magic class using animal forms, healing, ranged magic, or tanking.
record.Power_Basis: Nature power, shapeshifting, celestial cycles, and specialization.
record.Key_Distinction: Different playable peoples possess different druidic traditions and forms.
record.Source_Reference: Official World of Warcraft race and class reference pages, version-stamped 2026-08-01.

record.Ontology_or_Role_Summary: Spirit- and element-mediated class using totems, weapons, healing, and elemental attacks.
record.Power_Basis: Relationships with elements and spirits, totems, and specialization.
record.Key_Distinction: The class groups culturally distinct traditions under one game label.
record.Source_Reference: Official World of Warcraft race and class reference pages, version-stamped 2026-08-01.

record.Ontology_or_Role_Summary: Fel- and shadow-using class that summons demons and practices dangerous magic.
record.Power_Basis: Learned forbidden magic, summoned servants, soul resources, and specialization.
record.Key_Distinction: Unlike D&D warlocks, patron contracts are not the defining universal mechanic.
record.Source_Reference: Official World of Warcraft race and class reference pages, version-stamped 2026-08-01.

record.Ontology_or_Role_Summary: Light-using armored class with healing, protection, and damage specializations.
record.Power_Basis: Faith or Light discipline, armor, weapons, and orders.
record.Key_Distinction: Distinct cultures have different paladin institutions and theologies.
record.Source_Reference: Official World of Warcraft race and class reference pages, version-stamped 2026-08-01.

record.Ontology_or_Role_Summary: Stealth and precision class using poisons, subterfuge, blades, or outlaw techniques.
record.Power_Basis: Training, stealth, combo resources, and specialization.
record.Key_Distinction: It includes assassins and swashbucklers without making all rogues criminals.
record.Source_Reference: Official World of Warcraft race and class reference pages, version-stamped 2026-08-01.

record.Additional_Archetype_Names: Death-Knight Transformation; Dark Knight and Blackguard
record.Ontology_or_Role_Summary: Runeblade-using undead or death-empowered warrior class originating in coercive necromantic service.
record.Power_Basis: Undeath or death power, rune weapons, training, and liberation.
record.Key_Distinction: It crosses class, transformed state, and historical military order.
record.Source_Reference: Official World of Warcraft race and class reference pages, version-stamped 2026-08-01.

record.Ontology_or_Role_Summary: Martial occult class that internalizes demonic power to fight demons.
record.Power_Basis: Training, ritual mutation, fel power, mobility, and sacrifice.
record.Key_Distinction: The class embraces controlled corruption rather than remaining metaphysically untouched.
record.Source_Reference: Official World of Warcraft race and class reference pages, version-stamped 2026-08-01.

record.Ontology_or_Role_Summary: Dracthyr class using combined dragonflight magic for damage, augmentation, or healing.
record.Power_Basis: Engineered draconic nature, empowered spells, and specialization.
record.Key_Distinction: Initially race-linked and inseparable from dracthyr creation history.
record.Source_Reference: Official World of Warcraft race and class reference pages, version-stamped 2026-08-01.

nodes.label: Humans of the Empire and neighboring realms

record.Canonical_Name: Humans of the Empire and neighboring realms
record.Ontology_or_Role_Summary: Multiple human cultures organized into kingdoms, city-states, empires, and religious institutions.
record.Power_Basis: Natural ancestry, state, religion, and region.
record.Key_Distinction: Warhammer humans are not one class or moral faction.
record.Source_Reference: Games Workshop official Warhammer: The Old World setting and faction pages; detailed unit verification remains edition-specific.

record.Ontology_or_Role_Summary: Long-lived mountain and hold peoples defined by craft, memory, oaths, and ancestral grievances.
record.Power_Basis: Natural ancestry, clan/hold culture, engineering, and runes.
record.Key_Distinction: Spelling, metaphysics, and social codes are setting-specific.
record.Source_Reference: Games Workshop official Warhammer: The Old World setting and faction pages; detailed unit verification remains edition-specific.

record.Ontology_or_Role_Summary: Ulthuan-centered elven civilization with powerful magic, maritime influence, and internal politics.
record.Power_Basis: Natural ancestry, long life, magic, and state tradition.
record.Key_Distinction: ‘High’ denotes a historical-political identity, not objective superiority.
record.Source_Reference: Games Workshop official Warhammer: The Old World setting and faction pages; detailed unit verification remains edition-specific.

record.Ontology_or_Role_Summary: Forest-bound elven societies entangled with Athel Loren's spirits and dangers.
record.Power_Basis: Ancestry, forest pact, spirit relations, and isolation.
record.Key_Distinction: Not merely benevolent nature guardians.
record.Source_Reference: Games Workshop official Warhammer: The Old World setting and faction pages; detailed unit verification remains edition-specific.

record.Ontology_or_Role_Summary: Naggaroth-centered elven civilization shaped by schism, militarism, slavery, and sorcery.
record.Power_Basis: Shared elven ancestry plus historical and political divergence.
record.Key_Distinction: The label is cultural-political rather than a separate moral biology.
record.Source_Reference: Games Workshop official Warhammer: The Old World setting and faction pages; detailed unit verification remains edition-specific.

record.Ontology_or_Role_Summary: Large martial greenskins organized through warbands and dominance hierarchies.
record.Power_Basis: Distinct biology, collective energy, and war culture.
record.Key_Distinction: They are setting-specific fungal-like greenskins, not Tolkien orcs.
record.Source_Reference: Games Workshop official Warhammer: The Old World setting and faction pages; detailed unit verification remains edition-specific.

record.Ontology_or_Role_Summary: Smaller greenskins with varied subterranean, forest, and nomadic societies.
record.Power_Basis: Distinct biology, cunning, tribes, and ecology.
record.Key_Distinction: They are more varied than a single cowardly minion role.
record.Source_Reference: Games Workshop official Warhammer: The Old World setting and faction pages; detailed unit verification remains edition-specific.

record.Ontology_or_Role_Summary: Numerous ratmen organized through clans, subterranean cities, plague, sorcery, and unstable technology.
record.Power_Basis: Natural or corruptive ancestry, clan institutions, and warpstone.
record.Key_Distinction: They are a full civilization and apocalyptic threat, not generic beastfolk.
record.Source_Reference: Games Workshop official Warhammer: The Old World setting and faction pages; detailed unit verification remains edition-specific.

record.Ontology_or_Role_Summary: Multiple reptilian castes created or directed within the Great Plan of the Old Ones.
record.Power_Basis: Engineered spawning, caste, sacred mission, and ancient cities.
record.Key_Distinction: The umbrella includes distinct kinds such as Slann, Saurus, Skinks, and Kroxigor.
record.Source_Reference: Games Workshop official Warhammer: The Old World setting and faction pages; detailed unit verification remains edition-specific.

record.Ontology_or_Role_Summary: Chaos-tainted humanoid beast peoples organized in herds and hostile to ordered civilization.
record.Power_Basis: Mutation, birth, Chaos influence, and herd culture.
record.Key_Distinction: They are not equivalent to neutral animal-featured peoples in other settings.
record.Source_Reference: Games Workshop official Warhammer: The Old World setting and faction pages; detailed unit verification remains edition-specific.

record.Ontology_or_Role_Summary: Manifestations or entities of Chaos associated with distinct gods and emotional-metaphysical forces.
record.Power_Basis: Warp/Chaos substance, summoning, and patron alignment.
record.Key_Distinction: They are not necessarily biological species or Christian demons.
record.Source_Reference: Games Workshop official Warhammer: The Old World setting and faction pages; detailed unit verification remains edition-specific.

record.Ontology_or_Role_Summary: Mortals empowered, mutated, and armored through devotion to Chaos.
record.Power_Basis: Patronage, corruption, mutation, martial training, and gifts.
record.Key_Distinction: They cross profession, religious allegiance, and transformed state.
record.Source_Reference: Games Workshop official Warhammer: The Old World setting and faction pages; detailed unit verification remains edition-specific.

record.Ontology_or_Role_Summary: Vampiric lords ruling or commanding undead hosts through bloodline and necromancy.
record.Power_Basis: Vampirism, aristocratic lineage, necromancy, and state power.
record.Key_Distinction: Different bloodlines have different cultures and capabilities.
record.Source_Reference: Games Workshop official Warhammer: The Old World setting and faction pages; detailed unit verification remains edition-specific.

record.Ontology_or_Role_Summary: Ancient Nehekharan rulers, soldiers, and subjects returned in preserved undead forms.
record.Power_Basis: Necromantic catastrophe, funerary ritual, dynastic identity, and tomb cult.
record.Key_Distinction: They retain civilizational identity rather than functioning as generic necromancer puppets.
record.Source_Reference: Games Workshop official Warhammer: The Old World setting and faction pages; detailed unit verification remains edition-specific.

record.Ontology_or_Role_Summary: Large, hunger-centered peoples organized in tribes, kingdoms, mercenary bands, and trade networks.
record.Power_Basis: Natural ancestry, appetite, kinship, ecology, and migration.
record.Key_Distinction: The setting satirizes appetite and violence but still depicts a society.
record.Source_Reference: Games Workshop official Warhammer: The Old World setting and faction pages; detailed unit verification remains edition-specific.

record.Ontology_or_Role_Summary: Investigators and executioners combating heresy, cults, undead, and forbidden magic.
record.Power_Basis: Institutional authority, faith, weapons, investigation, and fear.
record.Key_Distinction: The archetype is morally ambiguous and prone to persecution.
record.Source_Reference: Games Workshop official Warhammer: The Old World setting and faction pages; detailed unit verification remains edition-specific.

record.Ontology_or_Role_Summary: Dwarfs who take a death-seeking oath to redeem perceived dishonor through impossible combat.
record.Power_Basis: Oath, shame, martial specialization, and social transformation.
record.Key_Distinction: ‘Slayer’ is an identity and condition, not only a monster-killing skill.
record.Source_Reference: Games Workshop official Warhammer: The Old World setting and faction pages; detailed unit verification remains edition-specific.

record.Ontology_or_Role_Summary: Bretonnian knights transformed or blessed through attainment of the Grail quest.
record.Power_Basis: Chivalric quest, divine favor, lineage, and martial training.
record.Key_Distinction: The role is embedded in a specific feudal and religious ideology.
record.Source_Reference: Games Workshop official Warhammer: The Old World setting and faction pages; detailed unit verification remains edition-specific.

record.Ontology_or_Role_Summary: Formally trained human magic user associated with a particular magical wind and imperial college.
record.Power_Basis: Education, licensing, magical wind, and military service.
record.Key_Distinction: Institutional control and specialized schools are central.
record.Source_Reference: Games Workshop official Warhammer: The Old World setting and faction pages; detailed unit verification remains edition-specific.

record.Ontology_or_Role_Summary: Armored clergy who combine preaching, combat, and divine battle prayers.
record.Power_Basis: Faith, ordination, weapon training, and miracles.
record.Key_Distinction: Unlike a generic paladin, the priestly office is explicit.
record.Source_Reference: Games Workshop official Warhammer: The Old World setting and faction pages; detailed unit verification remains edition-specific.

record.Power_Basis: Military enumeration, command, unit composition, alliance, logistics, and prestige.
record.Key_Distinction: It is not a character level or species category, and exact enumeration belongs to the source's military imagination.
record.Comparative_Notes: A useful bridge between epic army description and strategy-game unit taxonomy.
record.Source_Reference: Ādi and Udyoga/Bhīṣma Parvas; army enumeration and deployment.

Terms.Textual_Witness: BORI Critical Edition reference structure; Ganguli English translation reviewed at parva level
Terms.Sacred_Context_Caution: Preserve the source enumeration rather than treating the term as a generic army size.

record.Continuity: Critical-edition-oriented source pass; Ganguli English translation reviewed at parva level
record.Additional_Archetype_Names: Marriage Trial or Bridegroom/Bride Test; Witness and Public Recognition
record.Ontology_or_Role_Summary: A public process in which marriage selection is structured through choice, lineage, assembly, political alliance, and sometimes contest or test.
record.Power_Basis: Kinship politics, public recognition, agency, qualification, competition, and alliance.
record.Key_Distinction: It is not simply a tournament where a woman is a prize; specific episodes require close attention to agency and political context.
record.Comparative_Notes: A reusable institution linking marriage, succession, public trial, and interstate politics.
record.Source_Reference: Ādi Parva marriage narratives.

Terms.Textual_Witness: BORI Critical Edition reference structure; Ganguli English translation reviewed at parva level
Terms.Sacred_Context_Caution: Do not reduce to a tournament prize; agency, lineage, public recognition, and politics vary by episode.

record.Continuity: Critical-edition-oriented source pass; Ganguli English translation reviewed at parva level
record.Additional_Archetype_Names: Cosmic or Social Order; Kinship Blessing or Curse
record.Ontology_or_Role_Summary: Major figures face incompatible claims from kinship, rulership, teacher debt, friendship, oath, justice, compassion, and social order.
record.Power_Basis: Relationship, office, knowledge, intention, consequence, and circumstance.
record.Key_Distinction: The conflict cannot be represented faithfully as a simple alignment choice with one obviously correct answer.
record.Comparative_Notes: A central reusable archetype for morally dense fantasy that preserves legitimate competing obligations.
record.Source_Reference: Epic-wide; especially Udyoga, Bhīṣma, Droṇa, Karṇa, and Śānti Parvas.

record.Continuity: Critical-edition-oriented source pass; Ganguli English translation reviewed at parva level
record.Additional_Archetype_Names: Oathbound State; Sacred Oath; Adviser and Counselor
record.Ontology_or_Role_Summary: An elder guardian whose extraordinary vow enables dynastic continuity and moral authority while binding him to institutions and outcomes he cannot fully endorse.
record.Power_Basis: Vow, lineage duty, martial power, counsel, public recognition, and longevity.
record.Key_Distinction: This is a source-specific character pattern, not a claim that Bhīṣma is reducible to the normalized archetype.
record.Comparative_Notes: A major reference point for the elder whose virtue and tragedy arise from the same binding promise.
record.Source_Reference: Ādi, Udyoga, and Bhīṣma Parvas.

record.Continuity: Critical-edition-oriented source pass; Ganguli English translation reviewed at parva level
record.Additional_Archetype_Names: Hidden Royal or Secret Heir; Reciprocity and Debt; Kinship Blessing or Curse
record.Ontology_or_Role_Summary: A heroic rival whose hidden birth, gratitude, friendship, status wounds, generosity, and loyalty bind him to a doomed side despite conflicting knowledge and kinship.
record.Power_Basis: Gift-debt, friendship, honor, hidden lineage, social recognition, and personal choice.
record.Key_Distinction: This pattern must not erase Karna's individual contradictions or turn loyalty into simple moral virtue.
record.Comparative_Notes: A powerful comparative case for the noble adversary and indebted champion.
record.Source_Reference: Ādi, Udyoga, and Karṇa Parvas.

record.Continuity: Embedded textual unit and epic context; Sanskrit and translated text reviewed
record.Additional_Archetype_Names: Charioteer; Adviser and Counselor; Avatars and Incarnations
record.Ontology_or_Role_Summary: A divine figure serves as charioteer, envoy, strategist, friend, and revelatory counselor while declining a conventional combatant role in the central battle.
record.Power_Basis: Divine incarnation, friendship, counsel, political action, charioteer role, and revelation.
record.Key_Distinction: The pattern is not equivalent to a support class, passive deity, or mentor NPC.
record.Comparative_Notes: A distinctive union of service position, strategic agency, divine embodiment, and ethical instruction.
record.Source_Reference: Udyoga and Bhīṣma Parvas; Bhagavad Gītā context.

record.Continuity: Critical-edition-oriented source pass; Ganguli English translation reviewed at parva level
record.Additional_Archetype_Names: Prince, Princess, and Royal Heir; Recognition or Identity Test
record.Ontology_or_Role_Summary: A person of royal or divine lineage grows outside full recognition, with concealed parentage shaping status, loyalty, rivalry, and later revelation.
record.Power_Basis: Birth secrecy, tokens or testimony, social recognition, fosterage, lineage, and political consequence.
record.Key_Distinction: Recognition does not automatically repair a lifetime of social relations or determine moral allegiance.
record.Comparative_Notes: Deepens the hidden-heir archetype by emphasizing recognition as social and ethical, not only genealogical.
record.Source_Reference: Ādi and Udyoga Parvas; Karna-related lineage revelation.

record.Continuity: Critical-edition-oriented source pass; Ganguli English translation reviewed at parva level
record.Additional_Archetype_Names: Lots, Dice, Cards, or Fate Objects; Exact-Wording Contract; Exile as Ritual or Social State
record.Ontology_or_Role_Summary: A court-recognized game expands into the loss of wealth, sovereignty, freedom, kinship security, and status, producing exile and an unresolved legitimacy crisis.
record.Power_Basis: Manipulation, chance, legalistic terms, witness, honor, compulsion, and court power.
record.Key_Distinction: It is not merely a hero's gambling flaw or random inciting incident.
record.Comparative_Notes: A distinctive mechanism for dispossession through procedure rather than battlefield conquest.
record.Source_Reference: Sabhā Parva.

record.Continuity: Critical-edition-oriented source pass; Ganguli English translation reviewed at parva level
record.Additional_Archetype_Names: Dynasty; Kinship Blessing or Curse; Conflict of Duties
record.Ontology_or_Role_Summary: A vast war grows from succession, humiliation, dispossession, alliance, oath, teacher debt, kinship, and repeated failures of settlement.
record.Power_Basis: Dynastic claim, diplomacy, alliance, military mobilization, obligation, and accumulated grievance.
record.Key_Distinction: It is not reducible to good kingdom versus evil horde; most combatants are linked through kinship, teaching, or hospitality.
record.Comparative_Notes: A foundational model for civil war where relational density intensifies every battle.
record.Source_Reference: Udyoga through Śalya Parvas.

record.Continuity: Embedded textual unit; Sanskrit and translated text reviewed through Gītā Supersite
record.Additional_Archetype_Names: Cosmic or Social Order; Avatars and Incarnations
record.Ontology_or_Role_Summary: At the threshold of battle, a warrior's collapse opens into instruction about action, self, duty, death, discipline, devotion, knowledge, and divine reality.
record.Power_Basis: Dialogue, divine counsel, crisis, revelation, disciplined seeing, and choice.
record.Key_Distinction: It is not a pre-fight tutorial, morale buff, or simple command to obey.
record.Comparative_Notes: A major archetype for philosophical revelation embedded at the point of irreversible action.
record.Source_Reference: Bhagavad Gītā.

record.Continuity: Critical-edition-oriented source pass; Ganguli English translation reviewed at parva level
record.Additional_Archetype_Names: Sacred Kingship; Burial or Funeral Requirement; Sacred Battlefield
record.Ontology_or_Role_Summary: After victory, survivors confront mass death, mourning, funerary duty, guilt, justice, kingship, punishment, policy, and the burden of ruling what remains.
record.Power_Basis: Grief, counsel, law, ritual, memory, political office, and survivor responsibility.
record.Key_Distinction: Victory does not close the story or prove the war morally uncomplicated.
record.Comparative_Notes: A major corrective to fantasy narratives that omit aftermath, governance, and mourning.
record.Source_Reference: Strī, Śānti, and Anuśāsana Parvas.

record.Ontology_or_Role_Summary: The player selects a major god within a pantheon, establishing a civilization's initial divine identity, bonuses, god power, technologies, and later branching choices.
record.Power_Basis: Faction selection, deity portfolio, asymmetrical bonuses, technologies, and age-up branches.
record.Key_Distinction: This is a game system that factionalizes complex traditions; it is not a neutral map of historical religion.
record.Comparative_Notes: A key adaptation operation: pantheon becomes strategy faction and technology tree.
record.Source_Reference: Official Age of Mythology: Retold game and expansion reference pages.

record.Additional_Archetype_Names: Progression and Build Models; Divine Patronage or Favor
record.Ontology_or_Role_Summary: A top-level deity choice defines strategic bonuses, starting divine power, roster access, and the set of later minor-god branches.
record.Power_Basis: Player selection and game-defined divine portfolio.
record.Key_Distinction: The deity is represented as a rule package rather than a full mythological person or cultic tradition.
record.Comparative_Notes: Shows how divine patronage becomes a build-defining initial choice.
record.Source_Reference: Official Age of Mythology: Retold game and expansion reference pages.

record.Additional_Archetype_Names: Pantheon or Patron Choice; Cyclical-Age Law
record.Ontology_or_Role_Summary: Advancing to a new age requires choosing between minor gods that unlock technologies, myth units, and a god power.
record.Power_Basis: Age progression, patron branch, technology unlocks, and faction-specific roster.
record.Key_Distinction: Cosmic ages and divine plurality are converted into a permanent tech-tree branch.
record.Comparative_Notes: A clear case of progression abstraction and pantheon standardization.
record.Source_Reference: Official Age of Mythology: Retold game and expansion reference pages.

record.Additional_Archetype_Names: Favor Generation Model; Resource and Casting Models
record.Ontology_or_Role_Summary: Favor is accumulated through civilization-specific behaviors and spent principally on mythic units, divine technologies, and related content.
record.Power_Basis: Mechanized worship, combat, monuments, heroes, or other faction-specific generation methods.
record.Key_Distinction: Quantified favor is a game economy, not a faithful measure of devotion, ritual, or divine reciprocity.
record.Comparative_Notes: Demonstrates resource abstraction of religious relation.
record.Source_Reference: Official Age of Mythology: Retold game and expansion reference pages.

record.Additional_Archetype_Names: Divine Miracle; Divine Patronage or Favor
record.Ontology_or_Role_Summary: Divine intervention is represented as a targeted or global activated power with defined availability, effects, and strategic timing.
record.Power_Basis: Major/minor god selection, age progression, charges or recast rules, and player targeting.
record.Key_Distinction: The mechanic standardizes diverse divine actions into comparable abilities.
record.Comparative_Notes: A major example of mechanization and quantification of divine agency.
record.Source_Reference: Official Age of Mythology: Retold game and expansion reference pages.

record.Additional_Archetype_Names: Resource and Casting Models; Wonder Age or Overflow Phase
record.Ontology_or_Role_Summary: Some divine powers can be used again according to cooldown, resource, Wonder Age, or expansion-specific rules.
record.Power_Basis: Cooldown, game state, favor or age mechanics, and official balance design.
record.Key_Distinction: Recast rules are live-service mechanics, not mythological claims.
record.Comparative_Notes: Shows how divine intervention becomes part of a repeatable ability economy.
record.Source_Reference: Official Age of Mythology: Retold game and expansion reference pages.

record.Additional_Archetype_Names: Dragons and Legendary Beasts; Myth-Unit and Hero Counter Triangle
record.Ontology_or_Role_Summary: A mythological being is converted into a trainable combat unit with cost, population, counters, upgrades, and a defined place in the faction roster.
record.Power_Basis: Temple production, favor and resource costs, technology, age, and game balance.
record.Key_Distinction: Unitization can erase personhood, ambivalence, locality, or narrative uniqueness.
record.Comparative_Notes: The central bridge from mythological being to strategy-game unit taxonomy.
record.Source_Reference: Official Age of Mythology: Retold game and expansion reference pages.

record.Additional_Archetype_Names: Warrior or Fighter; Myth-Unit and Hero Counter Triangle
record.Ontology_or_Role_Summary: Heroes receive a distinct mechanical role, especially enhanced effectiveness against myth units and resistance to some mythic effects.
record.Power_Basis: Hero status, faction roster, counter design, and named or generic unit rules.
record.Key_Distinction: Heroism becomes a counter category rather than a full narrative biography.
record.Comparative_Notes: A strong example of counter-role assignment.
record.Source_Reference: Official Age of Mythology: Retold game and expansion reference pages.

record.Additional_Archetype_Names: Martial Roles; Myth-Unit and Hero Counter Triangle
record.Ontology_or_Role_Summary: Ordinary military units occupy the non-mythic portion of the roster and participate in a designed counter ecology with heroes and myth units.
record.Power_Basis: Resources, barracks or other production buildings, technologies, and counter stats.
record.Key_Distinction: The 'human' category is mechanical and can conceal historical, social, and factional complexity.
record.Comparative_Notes: Helps distinguish ordinary army roles from divine and heroic unit classes.
record.Source_Reference: Official Age of Mythology: Retold game and expansion reference pages.

record.Additional_Archetype_Names: Combat Function Archetypes; Elemental Opposition or Counter Law
record.Ontology_or_Role_Summary: The game assigns heroes specialized effectiveness against myth units within a broader web of unit counters.
record.Power_Basis: Damage bonuses, resistances, unit tags, and roster composition.
record.Key_Distinction: The relationship is tactical design, not a universal rule that heroes defeat monsters in source traditions.
record.Comparative_Notes: A paradigmatic example of adaptation through counter-role assignment.
record.Source_Reference: Official Age of Mythology: Retold game and expansion reference pages.

record.Ontology_or_Role_Summary: Relics are discovered, carried by heroes, placed in temples, and converted into persistent strategic bonuses.
record.Power_Basis: Map exploration, hero transport, temple custody, and bonus effects.
record.Key_Distinction: Sacred or legendary objects are itemized and standardized as collectible modifiers.
record.Comparative_Notes: Shows artifact-to-objective conversion and institutional simplification.
record.Source_Reference: Official Age of Mythology: Retold game and expansion reference pages.

record.Ontology_or_Role_Summary: The temple functions as a production and storage site for myth units, favor-related technology, and relics.
record.Power_Basis: Building placement, resource economy, unit production, and faction rules.
record.Key_Distinction: A complex ritual institution is reduced to a strategic building function.
record.Comparative_Notes: A useful case of institutional simplification without claiming equivalence.
record.Source_Reference: Official Age of Mythology: Retold game and expansion reference pages.

record.Additional_Archetype_Names: Divine and Celestial Beings; Boss Unit
record.Ontology_or_Role_Summary: A gigantic mythic being is represented as a limited strategic superunit requiring special progression and construction.
record.Power_Basis: Titan Gate, age or technology requirements, construction, population rules, and immense combat stats.
record.Key_Distinction: The game-mechanical category combines source-specific beings under a superunit role.
record.Comparative_Notes: A clear example of bossification and strategic escalation.
record.Source_Reference: Official Age of Mythology: Retold game and expansion reference pages.

record.Additional_Archetype_Names: Titan or Superunit Escalation; Summoned Threshold
record.Ontology_or_Role_Summary: A special project opens the way for a Titan to enter the battlefield.
record.Power_Basis: Construction, progression prerequisites, map placement, and game-state escalation.
record.Key_Distinction: The gate is a game-specific production mechanism, not a traditional cosmological object.
record.Comparative_Notes: Links portal device, summoned threshold, and superunit economy.
record.Source_Reference: Official Age of Mythology: Retold game and expansion reference pages.

record.Ontology_or_Role_Summary: A monumental Wonder unlocks a late-game age that accelerates god powers and mythic escalation beyond ordinary age progression.
record.Power_Basis: Wonder construction, age advancement, official rule set, and endgame economy.
record.Key_Distinction: The 'age' is a designed overflow phase rather than a historical or cosmological age.
record.Comparative_Notes: Exemplifies progression abstraction and monument mechanization.
record.Source_Reference: Official Age of Mythology: Retold game and expansion reference pages.

record.Ontology_or_Role_Summary: Greek mythological figures and beings are standardized into major gods, minor-god branches, heroes, myth units, technologies, and god powers.
record.Power_Basis: Official roster design, classical iconography, game balance, and adaptation history.
record.Key_Distinction: The roster is a commercial synthesis and not a primary source for Greek religion or myth.
record.Comparative_Notes: A comparison layer for how an already game-saturated tradition becomes a faction tree.
record.Source_Reference: Official Age of Mythology: Retold game and expansion reference pages.

record.Ontology_or_Role_Summary: Egyptian divine and mythic materials are translated into major-god choices, priest and pharaoh mechanics, monuments, myth units, and god powers.
record.Power_Basis: Official roster design, visual adaptation, faction economy, and counter system.
record.Key_Distinction: The faction compresses millennia of regional and historical variation into one strategy roster.
record.Comparative_Notes: A high-value case of temporal and regional standardization.
record.Source_Reference: Official Age of Mythology: Retold game and expansion reference pages.

record.Ontology_or_Role_Summary: Norse figures and beings are organized as major and minor gods, heroes, myth units, technologies, and a combat-linked favor economy.
record.Power_Basis: Official roster design, Eddic and popular imagery, faction economy, and game balance.
record.Key_Distinction: The roster should not be used as evidence for Old Norse categories or moral alignments.
record.Comparative_Notes: Shows how modern Viking imagery and mythic sources are recombined into strategy roles.
record.Source_Reference: Official Age of Mythology: Retold game and expansion reference pages.

record.Ontology_or_Role_Summary: The Atlantean faction combines a game-original civilization with selected Greek divine figures, Titan themes, heroized citizens, and campaign continuity.
record.Power_Basis: Franchise lore, Platonic and modern Atlantis reception, Greek deity roster, and game design.
record.Key_Distinction: It is not an ancient Atlantean religious tradition; the faction is explicitly composite and adaptation-driven.
record.Comparative_Notes: A valuable case of invented tradition, recombination, and pseudo-historical standardization.
record.Source_Reference: Official Age of Mythology: Retold game and expansion reference pages.

record.Ontology_or_Role_Summary: The expansion converts selected Chinese divine, immortal, legendary, and mythic materials into a standardized strategy roster and faction economy.
record.Power_Basis: Official expansion design, pantheon branches, myth units, technologies, and god powers.
record.Key_Distinction: The roster must not stand in for the plurality of Chinese religious, literary, regional, and historical traditions.
record.Comparative_Notes: A current example of commercial syncretism and celestial-bureaucracy adaptation.
record.Source_Reference: Official Age of Mythology: Retold game and expansion reference pages.

record.Ontology_or_Role_Summary: The expansion converts selected Japanese divine, heroic, spirit, and monster materials into major and minor gods, units, powers, and technologies.
record.Power_Basis: Official expansion design, Shinto- and folklore-derived imagery, faction mechanics, and game balance.
record.Key_Distinction: Kami, yōkai, historical figures, and later popular images must not be collapsed into one timeless pantheon.
record.Comparative_Notes: A strong case for analyzing purity, place, spirit, and deity concepts after unitization.
record.Source_Reference: Official Age of Mythology: Retold game and expansion reference pages.

record.Ontology_or_Role_Summary: The expansion adapts selected Mexica and Nahua divine, ritual, calendrical, warrior, and mythic materials into a strategy faction.
record.Power_Basis: Official expansion design, faction economy, divine choices, units, powers, and technologies.
record.Key_Distinction: The roster is not a complete or primary account of Mexica religion and must not be merged with Maya or generic Mesoamerican material.
record.Comparative_Notes: A high-priority case for examining ritual-economy abstraction and commercial pantheon construction.
record.Source_Reference: Official Age of Mythology: Retold game and expansion reference pages.

record.Additional_Archetype_Names: Branching Age-Up Choice; God-Power Ability Slot
record.Ontology_or_Role_Summary: God packs add alternative major-god choices, supporting minor-god branches, powers, technologies, and myth-unit access to existing pantheon structures.
record.Power_Basis: Downloadable content, official balance design, and extension of existing tech trees.
record.Key_Distinction: These are live-service roster expansions and require date-stamped maintenance.
record.Comparative_Notes: Shows how pantheons become modular content architectures.
record.Source_Reference: Official Age of Mythology: Retold game and expansion reference pages.

record.Additional_Archetype_Names: Hero and Protagonist Archetypes; Unique Character Class
record.Ontology_or_Role_Summary: Named protagonists move between narrative campaign roles and rule-defined hero units with scripted objectives and anti-myth capabilities.
record.Power_Basis: Campaign scripting, unit stats, narrative identity, and scenario progression.
record.Key_Distinction: The hero's narrative identity and mechanical counter role are related but not identical.
record.Comparative_Notes: Useful for crosswalking literary heroism into strategy-unit design.
record.Source_Reference: Official Age of Mythology: Retold game and expansion reference pages.

record.Additional_Archetype_Names: Worship or Favor Resource; Pantheon or Patron Choice
record.Ontology_or_Role_Summary: Each civilization produces favor through a thematically distinct method such as worship, combat, monuments, or hero activity.
record.Power_Basis: Faction rule, economic behavior, map interaction, and balance.
record.Key_Distinction: The thematic mechanism is a game interpretation, not a comparative theology.
record.Comparative_Notes: A concise example of cultural differentiation through resource mechanics.
record.Source_Reference: Official Age of Mythology: Retold game and expansion reference pages.

record.Ontology_or_Role_Summary: Mythological and historical ideas of eras are converted into a universal progression ladder with pantheon-specific branches.
record.Power_Basis: Resource thresholds, buildings, deity choice, technology unlocks, and strategic timing.
record.Key_Distinction: Shared age labels create comparability at the cost of source-specific temporal models.
record.Comparative_Notes: A high-value cross-media pattern linking cosmic age to technology tier.
record.Source_Reference: Official Age of Mythology: Retold game and expansion reference pages.

record.Continuity: Original game; base systems with DLC-aware notes, excluding Darkest Dungeon II
record.Additional_Archetype_Names: Resource and Casting Models; Expedition Trauma
record.Ontology_or_Role_Summary: A second damage economy accumulates through darkness, attacks, events, and expedition pressure and can trigger a crisis.
record.Power_Basis: Exposure, enemy abilities, environment, quirks, party interaction, and recovery.
record.Key_Distinction: Stress is mechanically independent from physical health and persists across expeditions.
record.Comparative_Notes: The source's major contribution is a campaign-scale psychological resource, not another conventional fantasy class.
record.Source_Reference: Darkest Dungeon official game overview and system documentation.

record.Continuity: Original game; base systems with DLC-aware notes, excluding Darkest Dungeon II
record.Ontology_or_Role_Summary: Reaching a stress crisis triggers a resolve test that changes the hero's behavior and capability.
record.Power_Basis: Accumulated stress, probability, hero state, and game rules.
record.Key_Distinction: The crisis is a discrete branching event rather than a linear debuff.
record.Comparative_Notes: A reusable breaking-point mechanic for horror and attrition games.
record.Source_Reference: Darkest Dungeon official game overview and system documentation.

record.Continuity: Original game; base systems with DLC-aware notes, excluding Darkest Dungeon II
record.Additional_Archetype_Names: Affliction-or-Virtue Branch; Madness or Altered Perception
record.Ontology_or_Role_Summary: A hero can enter a persistent harmful state such as paranoia, fear, irrationality, or masochistic behavior after a crisis.
record.Power_Basis: Stress threshold and resolve outcome.
record.Key_Distinction: Affliction is an acquired state, not the hero's moral essence or species trait.
record.Comparative_Notes: A source-specific model for mechanically consequential breakdown.
record.Source_Reference: Darkest Dungeon official game overview and system documentation.

record.Continuity: Original game; base systems with DLC-aware notes, excluding Darkest Dungeon II
record.Additional_Archetype_Names: Affliction-or-Virtue Branch; Empowerment, Bond, and Alignment States
record.Ontology_or_Role_Summary: A crisis can instead produce a beneficial state of exceptional resolve, focus, courage, or support.
record.Power_Basis: Stress threshold and favorable resolve outcome.
record.Key_Distinction: Virtue is a temporary crisis response, not a permanent alignment category.
record.Comparative_Notes: Pairs collapse and resilience within the same pressure system.
record.Source_Reference: Darkest Dungeon official game overview and system documentation.

record.Continuity: Original game; base systems with DLC-aware notes, excluding Darkest Dungeon II
record.Ontology_or_Role_Summary: Heroes acquire durable beneficial and harmful traits through expeditions, locations, treatment, and events.
record.Power_Basis: Experience, environmental interaction, random events, treatment, and locking/removal systems.
record.Key_Distinction: Quirks individualize roster members and create long-term friction; they are not temporary status effects.
record.Comparative_Notes: A strong emergent-biography system for replaceable adventurers.
record.Source_Reference: Darkest Dungeon official game overview and system documentation.

record.Continuity: Original game; base systems with DLC-aware notes, excluding Darkest Dungeon II
record.Ontology_or_Role_Summary: Diseases impose lasting penalties and require treatment or management across expeditions.
record.Power_Basis: Exposure, enemy attacks, events, and medical treatment.
record.Key_Distinction: Disease is one component of attrition and should not be conflated with curse, stress affliction, or corruption.
record.Comparative_Notes: Reinforces a multi-track model of adventurer vulnerability.
record.Source_Reference: Darkest Dungeon official game overview and system documentation.

record.Continuity: Original game; base systems with DLC-aware notes, excluding Darkest Dungeon II
record.Additional_Archetype_Names: Light and Radiance Magic; Expedition Attrition Loop
record.Ontology_or_Role_Summary: Torch level affects danger, stress, surprise, reward, and the emotional texture of an expedition.
record.Power_Basis: Consumable torches, exploration time, player risk choice, and environmental rules.
record.Key_Distinction: Light is not only visibility or a holy damage type; it is a strategic risk/reward meter.
record.Comparative_Notes: A distinctive use of illumination as campaign economy and player-controlled difficulty.
record.Source_Reference: Darkest Dungeon official game overview and system documentation.

record.Continuity: Original game; base systems with DLC-aware notes, excluding Darkest Dungeon II
record.Ontology_or_Role_Summary: Health, stress, supplies, light, disease, quirks, and other burdens accumulate over a dungeon expedition.
record.Power_Basis: Room sequence, combat, curios, food, torches, camping, and retreat decisions.
record.Key_Distinction: The meaningful unit is the whole expedition, not a series of fully reset encounters.
record.Comparative_Notes: A high-value pattern for survival-oriented dungeon design.
record.Source_Reference: Darkest Dungeon official game overview and system documentation.

record.Continuity: Original game; base systems with DLC-aware notes, excluding Darkest Dungeon II
record.Ontology_or_Role_Summary: Camping consumes supplies and uses hero-specific skills to heal, reduce stress, prepare, and manage risk during longer expeditions.
record.Power_Basis: Camping supplies, selected skills, time, party composition, and ambush rules.
record.Key_Distinction: Recovery remains limited and strategic rather than a complete reset.
record.Comparative_Notes: Combines party role identity with downtime decisions inside the expedition.
record.Source_Reference: Darkest Dungeon official game overview and system documentation.

record.Continuity: Original game; base systems with DLC-aware notes, excluding Darkest Dungeon II
record.Ontology_or_Role_Summary: Town institutions reduce stress through prayer, meditation, drinking, gambling, or other activities while making heroes temporarily unavailable.
record.Power_Basis: Gold, town facilities, character restrictions, time, and quirks.
record.Key_Distinction: The institutions are not merely heal buttons; they create cost, availability, and character-specific complications.
record.Comparative_Notes: A reusable model for social institutions as campaign recovery systems.
record.Source_Reference: Darkest Dungeon official game overview and system documentation.

record.Continuity: Original game; base systems with DLC-aware notes, excluding Darkest Dungeon II
record.Ontology_or_Role_Summary: A town institution treats disease and modifies persistent quirks through time and resource expenditure.
record.Power_Basis: Gold, facility upgrades, treatment slots, and hero availability.
record.Key_Distinction: Treatment changes long-term roster state rather than only restoring combat health.
record.Comparative_Notes: Connects character traits to institutional infrastructure.
record.Source_Reference: Darkest Dungeon official game overview and system documentation.

record.Continuity: Original game; base systems with DLC-aware notes, excluding Darkest Dungeon II
record.Additional_Archetype_Names: Roster-Based Campaign; Final Death or Soul Destruction
record.Ontology_or_Role_Summary: Heroes can die permanently, leaving the campaign to continue through the surviving and newly recruited roster.
record.Power_Basis: Combat outcome, expedition risk, retreat decisions, and limited exceptions.
record.Key_Distinction: The campaign persists after individual death; the roster, not one immortal protagonist, is the continuity anchor.
record.Comparative_Notes: Makes mortality a strategic and narrative system rather than a reload-only failure.
record.Source_Reference: Darkest Dungeon official game overview and system documentation.

record.Continuity: Original game; base systems with DLC-aware notes, excluding Darkest Dungeon II
record.Additional_Archetype_Names: Companion Collection System; Roster of Flawed Adventurers
record.Ontology_or_Role_Summary: The player recruits, rotates, treats, upgrades, specializes, and sometimes loses a large roster of adventurers.
record.Power_Basis: Stagecoach recruitment, town capacity, upgrades, stress, disease, quirks, and permadeath.
record.Key_Distinction: The heroes are neither disposable generic units nor one fixed party; individuals accumulate histories while remaining replaceable.
record.Comparative_Notes: A distinctive middle ground between tactics roster and literary protagonist ensemble.
record.Source_Reference: Darkest Dungeon official game overview and system documentation.

record.Continuity: Original game; base systems with DLC-aware notes, excluding Darkest Dungeon II
record.Ontology_or_Role_Summary: A hero's available skills and legal targets depend on current rank, making movement, disruption, and party order central.
record.Power_Basis: Formation rank, selected skills, movement, target rows, and enemy displacement.
record.Key_Distinction: Position determines capability, not only a small bonus.
record.Comparative_Notes: A major refinement of front-line/back-line roles into skill geometry.
record.Source_Reference: Darkest Dungeon official game overview and system documentation.

record.Continuity: Original game; base systems with DLC-aware notes, excluding Darkest Dungeon II
record.Ontology_or_Role_Summary: Dungeon corridors, rooms, encounters, curios, and rewards are assembled for repeated uncertain expeditions.
record.Power_Basis: Procedural generation, mission type, region, difficulty, and game state.
record.Key_Distinction: The procedural structure supports attrition and scouting rather than open-world randomness.
record.Comparative_Notes: A reusable link between megadungeon narrative and repeatable campaign logistics.
record.Source_Reference: Darkest Dungeon official game overview and system documentation.

record.Continuity: Original game; base systems with DLC-aware notes, excluding Darkest Dungeon II
record.Ontology_or_Role_Summary: The campaign begins because an ancestor's curiosity, wealth, bargains, excavations, and transgressions have corrupted an estate and surrounding region.
record.Power_Basis: Inherited property, forbidden knowledge, buried systems, social privilege, and supernatural consequence.
record.Key_Distinction: The player inherits responsibility and infrastructure, not personal guilt in a simple moral accounting.
record.Comparative_Notes: A strong modern form of ancestral folly as campaign premise.
record.Source_Reference: Darkest Dungeon official game overview and system documentation.

record.Continuity: Original game; base systems with DLC-aware notes, excluding Darkest Dungeon II
record.Ontology_or_Role_Summary: Heroes arrive with vulnerabilities, quirks, diseases, trauma, and distinctive combat roles, forming an unstable but persistent company.
record.Power_Basis: Recruitment, individual traits, class kits, shared expeditions, and recovery institutions.
record.Key_Distinction: The ensemble is not an idealized chosen party and no member is guaranteed narrative survival.
record.Comparative_Notes: A reusable model for emergent characterization through systemically vulnerable heroes.
record.Source_Reference: Darkest Dungeon official game overview and system documentation.

record.Continuity: Original game; base systems with DLC-aware notes, excluding Darkest Dungeon II
record.Additional_Archetype_Names: Stress Resource Track; Expedition Trauma; Inherited Ruin or Ancestor's Folly
record.Ontology_or_Role_Summary: Repeated descents into hostile ruins accumulate fear, obsession, stress, and loss while gradually revealing an inherited cosmic horror.
record.Power_Basis: Expedition repetition, stress, narrator framing, environmental revelation, and roster memory.
record.Key_Distinction: Mental pressure is structural rather than an occasional madness scene.
record.Comparative_Notes: The game's most distinctive narrative-mechanical contribution beyond its class roster.
record.Source_Reference: Darkest Dungeon official game overview and system documentation.

record.Continuity: Original game; base systems with DLC-aware notes, excluding Darkest Dungeon II
record.Additional_Archetype_Names: Stress Resource Track; Quirk Trait System
record.Ontology_or_Role_Summary: Heroes carry behavioral, psychological, and bodily consequences from dungeon experience into later missions and treatment.
record.Power_Basis: Stress, affliction, quirks, disease, survival, and recovery.
record.Key_Distinction: Trauma is represented through several linked systems rather than one universal diagnosis.
record.Comparative_Notes: A bridge between mechanical persistence and emergent character biography.
record.Source_Reference: Darkest Dungeon official game overview and system documentation.

record.Preserved_Dimension: Divine portfolio, name, iconography, and patron relation
record.Changed_or_Lost: Narrative, cult, regional history, ritual diversity, and theological ambiguity are compressed into bonuses and a tech tree.

record.Preserved_Dimension: Association with domains, beings, or divine powers
record.Changed_or_Lost: Religious plurality becomes a mutually exclusive upgrade branch with standardized timing.
record.Mechanical_Function: Unlocks myth units, technologies, and a god power
record.Source_Reference: Age of Mythology: Retold official game and expansion materials.

record.Preserved_Dimension: Spectacle, divine attribution, and exceptional effect
record.Changed_or_Lost: Context, petition, moral ambiguity, ritual process, and divine autonomy are converted into player targeting and cooldown/charge rules.
record.Mechanical_Function: Produces battlefield, economic, environmental, or summoning effects
record.Source_Reference: Age of Mythology: Retold official game and expansion materials.

record.Preserved_Dimension: A relationship between community and divine power
record.Changed_or_Lost: Multiple forms of ritual, devotion, reciprocity, institution, and belief become one spendable numerical resource.
record.Mechanical_Function: Pays for myth units, divine technologies, and related effects
record.Source_Reference: Age of Mythology: Retold official game and expansion materials.

record.Traditional_Record_Type: Narrative person / lineage figure / cultic figure
record.Preserved_Dimension: Exceptional identity and opposition to monsters or divine threats
record.Changed_or_Lost: Biography, ritual status, tragedy, political role, and moral complexity are subordinated to a combat tag.
record.Mechanical_Function: Counters myth units and performs special objective functions

record.Traditional_Record_Type: Profession, social order, or historical unit
record.Preserved_Dimension: Weapons, broad tactical function, and factional identity
record.Changed_or_Lost: Training, status, logistics, historical change, and social institutions become standardized unit stats.
record.Mechanical_Function: Provides the ordinary army and participates in counter relationships
record.Source_Reference: Age of Mythology: Retold official game and expansion materials.

record.Preserved_Dimension: Sense of advancement and changing capability
record.Changed_or_Lost: Source-specific time models become a universal four-step economic and military ladder.
record.Mechanical_Function: Unlocks buildings, units, technologies, and minor-god choices
record.Source_Reference: Age of Mythology: Retold official game and expansion materials.

record.Preserved_Dimension: Sacred building identity and relation to divine powers
record.Changed_or_Lost: Ritual specialists, calendars, offerings, social authority, local history, and architectural variation are reduced to production functions.
record.Mechanical_Function: Produces myth units, researches technologies, and stores relics
record.Source_Reference: Age of Mythology: Retold official game and expansion materials.

record.Preserved_Dimension: Rarity, sacred or legendary aura, and hero association
record.Changed_or_Lost: Provenance, ritual custody, narrative uniqueness, contested authenticity, and restrictions are standardized.
record.Mechanical_Function: Heroes carry relics to temples for persistent bonuses
record.Source_Reference: Age of Mythology: Retold official game and expansion materials.

record.Preserved_Dimension: Scale, ancient power, and catastrophic presence
record.Changed_or_Lost: Genealogy, plurality, cosmic role, and individual narrative become one strategic category.
record.Mechanical_Function: Provides decisive late-game combat power
record.Source_Reference: Age of Mythology: Retold official game and expansion materials.

record.Preserved_Dimension: Sense of opening a passage for a primordial being
record.Changed_or_Lost: Ritual, cosmic law, divine conflict, and source geography become a construction project.
record.Mechanical_Function: Summons or enables a Titan superunit
record.Source_Reference: Age of Mythology: Retold official game and expansion materials.

record.Preserved_Dimension: Scale, prestige, civilization identity, and sacred symbolism
record.Changed_or_Lost: Historical function, labor, ritual, and contested meaning become a standardized strategic objective.
record.Mechanical_Function: Supports victory conditions and the Wonder Age
record.Source_Reference: Age of Mythology: Retold official game and expansion materials.

record.Preserved_Dimension: Recognizable deity names and domain associations
record.Changed_or_Lost: Fluid, local, historical, and overlapping relations are made exhaustive, balanced, and hierarchically selectable.
record.Mechanical_Function: Creates comparable faction architecture
record.Source_Reference: Age of Mythology: Retold official game and expansion materials.

record.Preserved_Dimension: Visual identity and one or two signature capacities
record.Changed_or_Lost: Ambivalence, hospitality, locality, kinship, ritual role, and noncombat meanings may disappear.
record.Mechanical_Function: Clarifies battlefield role and counter readability
record.Source_Reference: Age of Mythology: Retold official game and expansion materials.

record.Traditional_Concept: Kami, yōkai, heroes, ritual purity, and sacred place

record.Preserved_Dimension: Recognizable associations among gods, beings, powers, and symbols
